record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For bipartite quantum states, call two density operators equally entangled when they differ only by local choices of basis, meaning there are local unitaries UA and UB with rho = (UA tensor UB) sigma (UA tensor UB)*. A polynomial entanglement invariant is a real-valued local-unitary invariant polynomial in the matrix elements of the density operator. Are polynomial entanglement invariants complete, so that if all polynomial invariants of rho and sigma agree, rho and sigma must be related by such local unitaries?

evidence.quote:
The basic problem is to decide the following question:
• Are the polynomial entanglement invariants complete?,
i. e., if all polynomial invariants of ρ and σ agree, can we infer the existence of unitaries UA, UB satisfying the above equation?
The basic question of principle (are the polynomial entanglement invariants complete?) is answered in Onishchik and Vinberg’s book Lie Groups and Algebraic Groups

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, and consider density operators on $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$, i.e. positive semidefinite operators of trace one. Two density operators $\rho$ and $\sigma$ on $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ are called locally unitarily equivalent if there exist unitary operators $U_A$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $U_B$ on $\mathcal{H}_B$ such that
$$\rho = (U_A \otimes U_B)\, \sigma\, (U_A \otimes U_B)^*.$$
A polynomial entanglement invariant is a real-valued polynomial $p$ in the (real and imaginary parts of the) matrix entries of a density operator that is invariant under all local unitary transformations $(U_A \otimes U_B)\cdot(\,\cdot\,)\cdot(U_A \otimes U_B)^*$.

Question: Is the family of all polynomial entanglement invariants complete in the sense that, for any two density operators $\rho$ and $\sigma$ on $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$, the equality $p(\rho) = p(\sigma)$ for every polynomial entanglement invariant $p$ implies that $\rho$ and $\sigma$ are locally unitarily equivalent?
artifact.status_search_result: The completeness question is answered affirmatively by a classical theorem of Onishchik and Vinberg stating that orbits of a compact linear group on a real vector space are separated by polynomial invariants. Applied to the action of local unitaries on bipartite density operators, this yields completeness of the polynomial entanglement invariants. Concrete complete sets have also been worked out (e.g., Makhlin's 18 invariants for two qubits, and complete sets for arbitrary-dimensional bipartite states in subsequent work).

status_evidence.title: Polynomial entanglement invariants – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: The fundamental completeness question has been answered affirmatively... orbits of a compact linear group acting in a real vector space are separated by the polynomial invariants.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as solved; completeness follows from a theorem of Onishchik and Vinberg.

status_evidence.title: Local Unitary Equivalence of Arbitrary Dimensional Bipartite Mixed Quantum States
status_evidence.snippet: A complete set of invariants is presented such that two density matrices are local unitary equivalent if and only if all these invariants have equal values.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit complete sets of polynomial LU invariants are known for bipartite mixed states.
